test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
**Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:**

The annual report has been submitted by the audit department after multiple revisions.

options.text: The audit department submitted the annual report after multiple revisions.
The audit department is submitting the annual report after multiple revisions.
The audit department has submitted the annual report after multiple revisions.
The audit department had submitted the annual report after multiple revisions.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **present perfect tense** of the passive voice ("has been submitted").
 
• To convert a sentence from passive to active voice, the **agent** of the action ("the audit department") becomes the **subject**, and the original subject ("the annual report") becomes the **object**.
 
• The tense must remain consistent during the conversion. The present perfect active form is **"has/have + past participle."**
 
• Option 3 correctly maintains the present perfect tense and shifts the focus to the audit department.

Therefore, the correct answer is **The audit department has submitted the annual report after multiple revisions**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The audit department **has submitted** the annual report after multiple revisions."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Simple Past):** "submitted" changes the tense from present perfect to past tense, which alters the original meaning.
 
• **Option 2 (Present Continuous):** "is submitting" indicates an action currently in progress, which is not what the original sentence conveys.
 
• **Option 4 (Past Perfect):** "had submitted" refers to an action completed before another past action, which is a different tense entirely.
